label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. With a UCLA-8 loneliness mean of 1.74, PHQ-9 depression mean of 1.75, and notably high GAD-7 anxiety mean of 2.17, this group consistently scores above average on all three distress indicators. The combination of extensive screen time and graduate-level education suggests individuals who may be heavily engaged in digital work or social environments yet experience significant emotional isolation and psychological burden.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness despite likely high digital connectivity
Highest anxiety levels among profiles (GAD-7 mean 2.17)
Extended daily screen time of more than 5 hours
High educational attainment suggesting professional or academic engagement
tone: Anxious, emotionally burdened, and socially disconnected despite digital immersion

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They demonstrate strong psychological well-being across all three measured dimensions, with anxiety scores near floor level and depression and loneliness scores well below typical thresholds of concern.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77, well below clinical concern)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.33)
Moderate and controlled daily screen or internet usage (1–3 hours)
Highly educated, suggesting stable occupational or academic engagement

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they appear to manage their emotional well-being without significant clinical distress, suggesting a degree of psychological resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders even in the presence of perceived social isolation.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level or higher education, reporting 1–3 hours of daily screen time or social media use
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating moderate-to-high perceived social isolation
Low depressive symptom burden (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) well below clinical thresholds
Low anxiety symptom burden (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) well below clinical thresholds
Moderate and controlled digital engagement (1–3 hours daily)
Possible reliance on internal coping strategies or academic/professional engagement that mitigates mood deterioration despite social disconnection
tone: Quietly reflective and self-contained; socially understimulated but emotionally stable
